name: stitch-via
prompt: Stitch my tagged ground pour with the substrate's standard via on a 2 mm grid. Does it matter whether I pass the via class straight from the JLCPCB substrate, re-declare it on my own substrate class, or declare it at module scope? Build each and count the vias.

inputs.environment: Commands run from the repository root with python3 resolving to the project interpreter that has jitx installed and a reachable runtime; the check script is run once per variant from a project that packages the reference module.

expected_output: Three designs differing only in how the via class is declared, plus a control with no rule, each built and captured; the check compares the captured counts against the recorded measurements of nine for the rule variants and zero for the control. A separate regression compares the pad-edge count law against the original and discriminating measured rows recorded in the jitxexamples.patterns.stitch_via module docstring, reading pad diameter from the selected via class. Every mismatch exits nonzero.

assertions.text: the reference module type-checks against the installed jitx package
the pad-edge law matches recorded measurements, including rows where the center law predicts the wrong count
each rule variant produces the recorded nine vias and the control produces zero
assertions.cmd: for v in mixin direct module control; do python3 skills/jitx-layout-constraints/evals/cases/reference/stitch-via/check_stitch_via.py $v || exit 1; done

assertions.text: the stitch rule is a one-condition rule with stitch_via on a tagged pour, and the answer about via-class declaration is stated as verified on the named build, not assumed
